holes: state-ownership.md § `WorldCell` (STATE-D6): the frozen `vmMain` body unconditionally does `unsafe { (*WORLD.0.get()).as_mut().expect("GAME_INIT built the world") }` before calling `dispatch(command, world, ...)` for EVERY command, including `GAME_INIT` itself. But `WORLD` starts as `WorldCell::new()` = `UnsafeCell<None>`, and nothing in the frozen skeleton shows GAME_INIT writing `Some(GameWorld)` into the cell before that `.expect()` runs — so a literal transcription panics on the very first call. Raven's C original never has this problem (g_entities/level are already-existing zero-initialized static storage that G_InitGame just memsets, oracle/oracle/codemp/game/g_main.c:978-984), so there's no oracle precedent to copy for the Rust bootstrap step. The doc needs either a GAME_INIT-special-cased branch in vmMain (write-then-fallthrough) or an explicit `GameWorld::new`/lazy-construct convention, and it has neither.

state-ownership.md's WorldCell section and engine-seam.md's SEAM-D8 `Dispatch<C>` trait (`fn dispatch(&self, args: C::Args) -> C::Output`) don't compose for any mutating command. `GAME_RUN_FRAME`/`GAME_CLIENT_THINK`/`GAME_CLIENT_BEGIN`/etc. all mutate `level`/`entities` every call (oracle: g_main.c:3582 et al.), but `Dispatch<C>::dispatch` only gets `&self` (confirmed against the actual in-tree `GameRunFrame`/`GameInit` `InboundVmCall` impls at crates/mp/abi/src/game/vmcalls/{GAME_INIT,GAME_RUN_FRAME}.rs, which are exactly the `C` type parameters `impl Dispatch<C> for GameWorld` would be written against). engine-seam.md explicitly punts 'the Self receiver each Dispatch<C> impl reads/writes ... is not frozen here: it is the module-side state-ownership spine' to this doc, but state-ownership.md's WorldCell section never actually reconciles the immutable `&self` bound with the mutation requirement, and STATE-D1 explicitly forbids the interior-mutability escape hatches (no `RefCell`, no effect queues) that would normally paper over this. A porter hits a real, immediate compile-time contradiction implementing the very first `Dispatch<GameRunFrame> for GameWorld` impl.

No construction/zero-initialization mechanism is specified for the `#[repr(C)]`, non-`Default`, pointer-bearing types the frozen `GameWorld` struct heap-allocates: `Box<[gentity_t; MAX_GENTITIES]>` (1832B * 1024 ≈ 1.83MB, confirmed via the existing size_of assert at crates/mp/qshared/src/common/mp/gentity.rs:456) and `Box<[gclient_t; MAX_CLIENTS]>` (7344B * 32 ≈ 230KB, crates/mp/game/src/client/gclient.rs:234), plus `level_locals_t` itself. None of these types derive `Default` anywhere in-tree, and grepping the whole `crates/` tree turns up zero precedent for `Box<[T; N]>` construction, `MaybeUninit`, or `mem::zeroed` usage to model against. Raven's equivalent (`g_entities`/`g_clients`/`level`) are C statics that are simply memset in place (g_main.c:978-984) — never heap-allocated at runtime — so there is no oracle idiom to port faithfully; naively stack-building a ~1.83MB array before boxing it risks overflow on constrained-stack targets (e.g. 1MB default Windows threads). The doc's construction-order note (§ `GameWorld`) only fixes the *order* (allocate before wiring `level.gentities`/`level.clients`), not the *mechanism*.

To write a compiling GAME_INIT arm at all, I would have to invent a bootstrap convention not licensed by the frozen text — e.g. special-casing `command == GAME_INIT` in `vmMain` to build a `GameWorld` value and `.get_or_insert()`/write it into `WORLD` before falling into the generic dispatch path, rather than reading this off the doc.

To let `GAME_RUN_FRAME`/`GAME_CLIENT_*` mutate `GameWorld` despite `Dispatch<C>::dispatch(&self, ...)`'s immutable receiver, I would have to invent a resolution the doc doesn't sanction — e.g. reinterpreting `Self` as the raw `*mut GameWorld` (unsafe-dereferencing to `&mut` inside the impl body) rather than `GameWorld` itself, or having the free `dispatch()` router bypass the `Dispatch<C>` trait entirely for mutating commands. Either is a real design choice STATE-D1's 'no RefCell, no effect queues' constraint doesn't rule in or out, and neither this doc nor engine-seam.md picks one.

To heap-allocate the boxed entity/client arrays and `level_locals_t` safely, I would have to invent a zero-initialization idiom (e.g. `Box<MaybeUninit<[gentity_t; N]>>` + `alloc_zeroed` + `assume_init`, justified as mirroring Raven's static zero-init) that porting-rules §D11 ('unsafe confined to the seam') doesn't clearly license for this call site, since GameWorld construction is a step removed from the raw trap seam itself.

ModuleRegistry slot-shape conflicts with the engine-seam.md standing doc. module-loading.md freezes mp_engine_qcommon::ModuleRegistry with slot element Option<LoadedModule> where LoadedModule = { lib, entry } (module-loading.md:325-329, :434-436). engine-seam.md's state table (engine-seam.md:184, SEAM-D11) freezes the SAME mp_engine_qcommon::ModuleRegistry with a per-slot EngineSlot.engine (*mut Engine) trampoline cell — 'one cell per module slot'. The two frozen slot-element types (LoadedModule vs EngineSlot) are incompatible: a dry-run/porter following module-loading.md verbatim builds a ModuleRegistry whose slots cannot hold SEAM-D11's required per-slot engine cell. Resolving requires changing module-loading.md's frozen ModuleRegistry/LoadedModule struct (or reconciling LOAD-D8 against SEAM-D11), i.e. altering a settled decision, so it escalates to a session rather than self-resolving. Suggested reconciliation direction (not decided here): the per-slot element becomes one composed struct owning lib + entry + vm->name (Finding A) + the SEAM-D11 engine cell, with module-loading.md and engine-seam.md agreeing on that one type's name and fields.

`## Seam definition` freezes an SP `ModuleSearchPolicy` value that the doc's own decisions say is never constructed. module-loading.md:306-316 gives an 'SP policy (crates/sp/app caller)' — `CwdRelative` jagamex86.dll lookup — as a frozen Seam value a porter builds. But LOAD-D5 + DEC-07 + the state-ownership row (module-loading.md:204: 'our SP is fully static (DEC-07) → no handle ... has no parity-matrix row') state SP NEVER exercises the loader: jagame is reached through the `GetGameAPI` table factory, not `sys_load_dll`'s dllEntry/vmMain handshake, and the retail SP load-from-DLL variant is explicitly not ported. So the frozen SP `ModuleSearchPolicy` describes a construction site (crates/sp/app) that per the doc's decisions does not exist. Either the SP policy block should be removed from the frozen Seam (its search order belongs only in `## Raven ground truth`), or a decision is needed on the out-of-scope SP-DLL-hosting scenario it implies. Flagged rather than edited because deleting frozen Seam content is a design call, not a mechanical fix.
holes: LOAD-D8 (`ModuleRegistry::load_module`'s VM_Create-faithful slot-reuse-by-name) requires comparing the requested module name against each occupied slot's already-loaded name (oracle `qcommon/vm.cpp:485-489`: `if (!Q_stricmp(vmTable[i].name, module)) { vm = &vmTable[i]; return vm; }` — verified by reading vm.cpp directly). But the FROZEN `LoadedModule { lib: libloading::Library, entry: RawVmMain }` and `ModuleRegistry { slots: [Option<LoadedModule>; MAX_VM] }` shapes in ‘## Seam definition’ carry no field anywhere to store the name a slot was loaded with. I cannot write `load_module`'s reuse-scan without either widening one of these two structs (which the doc says are FROZEN, 'porters fill bodies without changing them') or silently dropping the cited reuse behavior (which porting-rules §A2 forbids). The doc needs to say where the name lives — e.g. `LoadedModule.name: String`, or a parallel `names: [Option<String>; MAX_VM]` on `ModuleRegistry` — and neither is specified or hinted at anywhere in the doc.

LOAD-D9's own code sample for the MP `ModuleSearchPolicy` unconditionally pushes the `fs_cdpath` `SearchStep::FsPath` step (`steps: vec![ FsPath{fs_basepath...}, FsPath{fs_cdpath...} ]`), annotated inline `// :859; skipped if empty` — but reading oracle `win_main.cpp:855-873` directly shows the cdpath probe is only ever attempted inside `if (cdpath[0]) { ... }`; an empty cdpath means the probe never runs and `Sys_LoadDll` returns `NULL` right after the basepath probe fails. The doc's own inline comment names the correct Raven behavior but the code sample it sits next to does not implement it, and the doc never says which layer is responsible for the skip: `native/platform::sys_load_dll` checking `base.as_os_str().is_empty()` before attempting a step (keeping `mp_engine_qcommon` simple but adding emptiness-awareness to the 'mechanism' crate LOAD-D1 says stays generic over the policy value), or the `mp_engine_qcommon` caller conditionally omitting the cdpath step from `steps` when the resolved cvar is empty (keeping `sys_load_dll` naive but requiring the caller to special-case one of its two pushed steps). Both are plausible and the choice changes which crate's code a porter writes.

VM_Create's earliest `Com_Error(ERR_FATAL, "VM_Create: bad parms")` guard (oracle `qcommon/vm.cpp:481`, `if (!module || !module[0] || !systemCalls)`) is absent from both the doc's ‘Raven ground truth’ section and LOAD-D11, which only enumerates the slot-full fatal (`vm.cpp:499-500`) as the one ERR_FATAL `load_module` reproduces via `com_error`. `load_module`'s frozen signature takes `name: &str` (an empty string is reachable) and `syscall: RawSyscall` (a null `*const c_void` is representable), so this Raven fatal path is reachable through the Rust API surface the doc froze, yet the doc gives no disposition for it — faithfully reproduce it as a second `com_error(ERR_FATAL, ...)` guard, treat it as statically unreachable and skip it, or mark it `//TODO: Port` — and I can't tell which from the doc.

To actually write `ModuleRegistry::load_module`'s body I would have had to silently add a `name` field somewhere not authorized by the FROZEN struct shapes — most likely `LoadedModule.name: String` alongside `lib`/`entry` — rather than getting that placement decision from the doc.

To implement the cdpath 'skipped if empty' behavior cited by LOAD-D9's own comment I would have had to silently decide that `sys_load_dll` (not the `mp_engine_qcommon` caller) checks `base.as_os_str().is_empty()` before attempting an `FsPath` step, since that keeps the frozen `sys_load_dll(policy, name, syscall)` signature unchanged — a plausible but undictated choice between two structurally different owners for the same behavior.

Field visibility for `LoadedModule.lib`/`.entry` and `SlotId`'s tuple field: the doc's code blocks show them with no visibility modifier, but the pinned one-type-per-file split (`loaded_module.rs` vs the constructing code in `loader.rs`; `slot_id.rs` vs `module_registry.rs`) forces some non-private visibility (`pub(super)`/`pub(in module_loader)`) that the doc never states — treated as ordinary Rust-idiom latitude (porting-rules §D12 'internal-only types get idiomatic shape'), not reported as a hole, but still an invented micro-decision every porter touching these files will make independently and possibly inconsistently.
defects: Frozen registry cannot implement its own frozen reuse-by-name semantics (Gate 2 — seam can't round-trip cited behavior). LOAD-D8 / `## Seam definition` freezes `ModuleRegistry::load_module` to 'reuse a live slot whose module name matches (vm.cpp:485-489, Q_stricmp(vmTable[i].name, module))' and lists first-free / slot-full branches. But the frozen structs store NO name: `ModuleRegistry { slots: [Option<LoadedModule>; MAX_VM] }` (module-loading.md:434-436), `LoadedModule { lib, entry }` (module-loading.md:325-329), `SlotId(u32)` is a bare index (module-loading.md:432). Raven's vm_t has `char name[MAX_QPATH]` (vm_local.h) precisely so the reuse scan works; the port dropped it. A porter filling `load_module` has nothing to compare against for the reuse-by-name branch. Cannot fix without deciding where/how the name is stored (add a `name` field to the FROZEN `LoadedModule`/`ModuleRegistry`, or decide reuse-by-name is unreachable and drop the branch) — a design micro-decision.

`load_module`'s not-found path is undefined and contradicts `sys_load_dll`'s own contract (Gate 2 — fork no decision covers). `sys_load_dll(...) -> Option<LoadedModule>` (module-loading.md:342) returns `None` when the artifact isn't found, and its doc-comment (module-loading.md:340-341) delegates: 'None = not found ... the caller decides fatal-vs-skip per mode.' Its only caller, `ModuleRegistry::load_module -> SlotId`, is frozen INFALLIBLE (LOAD-D11) with no failure channel, so it cannot surface `None` to any mode-specific caller, and the doc never states what `load_module` does when a fresh-slot `sys_load_dll` returns `None`. LOAD-D8/LOAD-D11 address only the slot-FULL fatal (com_error), never the not-FOUND case (Raven's path there is the out-of-scope QVM fallback, DEC-05.4, so 'faithful' is undefined for native-only MP). Resolving requires a decision (e.g. com_error(ERR_FATAL/ERR_DROP) on not-found, or widening the frozen infallible return) — it touches LOAD-D11's settled infallible `-> SlotId`.

com_printf crate home is a layering contradiction (§ Seam lines ~525-526, 552; LIFE-D2 amendment line ~848). The doc places `com_printf` in `mp_engine_core` ('Raven's most-called primitive rides up to the facade crate with Engine' ... 'threads &mut Engine, so per STATE-D5 it lives in mp_engine_core, not qcommon'). But `mp_engine_core` is the facade that DEPENDS ON qcommon/server/client (workspace-architecture.md:122,170-173 — 'the aggregate facade ... depends on the other mp/engine/* subcrates'); those tiers sit BELOW core and, as the doc itself states for STATE-Q4, 'do not depend on the core facade.' Raven's `Com_Printf` is called from 330 sites in mp qcommon (non-common.cpp) and 97 in mp server (grep-confirmed) — 427 lower-tier call sites that cannot name a `com_printf` defined in core. The design as written cannot compile: any ported server/qcommon function that prints has no path to `com_printf`. This is the IDENTICAL layering constraint the doc resolved for `com_error` by relocating it one tier down to `mp_engine_qcommon` (STATE-Q4 / LIFE-D2 amendment, applied precisely because 'leaf throw sites in mp_engine_server ... can raise it'); `com_printf` has the same constraint, far more pervasively, but is left in core with inconsistent reasoning (com_error was made receiverless and pushed down to be reachable; com_printf is kept up on the grounds that it threads &mut Engine — yet its callers below core cannot reach it regardless). Resolving requires a design decision on com_printf's home (the natural mirror of com_error is qcommon, with its Common-owned print target — rd_buffer/logfile/console per common.cpp:128,137-171 — living where the leaf callers can reach it). SAME CLASS, SMALLER: LIFE-D3 ports `sys_error` INTO `mp_engine_core`, but `Sys_Error` has 4 lower-tier callers (mp server x1, mp qcommon non-common x3) that likewise cannot reach a core-located `sys_error`; the doc should confirm whether those are re-routed through com_error(ERR_FATAL) or whether sys_error must also live below core.
